tasks.title: Document GUI/desktop tools wanted on every new machine
tasks.notes:
Gap between 'configs symlinked' and 'machine actually ready'. Start as docs/tools.md (tool, why, install command per package manager) rather than install.sh logic - package names differ across zypper/apt/pacman, flatpak-vs-native is a per-machine call, and install.sh assuming a package manager cuts against the minimal-dependencies principle. Promote into the installer later if the list stabilizes. Same shape as nvim-lazygit.

Scope now covers CLI tools too, not just GUI/desktop - suggest two sections in docs/tools.md, since the CLI half is natively packaged and scriptable and could plausibly be promoted into install.sh, while GUI stays a per-machine judgment call.

GUI entries: DBeaver (settled - go-to SQL GUI, flatpak io.dbeaver.DBeaverCommunity). S3/cloud storage GUI slot resolved as 'no GUI needed' - S3Drive evaluated and rejected (paywalled multi-file download, and unwilling to hand AWS creds to a freemium client); FileZilla Pro and Cyberduck/duck not pursued since aws-cli covers file moves and rclone covers the rest.

CLI entries (all installed and working as of 2026-07-28): aws-vault v7.2.0 for credentials - NOT packaged for openSUSE, install the binary from GitHub releases; uses AWS_VAULT_BACKEND=file (encrypted store at ~/.awsvault/keys) rather than the KWallet/Secret Service default, so the creds stay isolated from the desktop keyring. rclone for S3 - configure the remote with env_auth=true so it reads from aws-vault instead of storing its own copy, and 'rclone mount --vfs-cache-mode full' makes the bucket a normal directory that any tool (duckdb included) can read. duckdb for parquet - see duckdb-setup.

tasks.title: Split bootstrap into private repo depending on public dotfiles
tasks.notes: Two repos along a privacy line, dependency points one way only: PUBLIC dotfiles (configs, symlinks, install.sh - self-contained, useful to a stranger, never learns bootstrap exists) <- PRIVATE bootstrap (clones dotfiles, runs ./install.sh, then packages + private repos + per-repo setup). Why this works: keeps dotfiles genuinely publishable rather than publishable-with-holes, and confines the non-idempotent cloning/setup-script mess to the private repo so install.sh keeps its symlink-only idempotency. Precedent set: bootstrap orchestrates dotfiles via its existing clean ./install.sh entrypoint - suggests other repos (claude-toolkit, claude-sessions, schema-smith) should expose the same, rather than bootstrap knowing their internals. Publishability checked 2026-07-27: no work identifiers, hardcoded home paths, or credential-shaped strings in tracked files; .gitconfig NOT reviewed (secrets-guard hook) - check it for email/signing key/includeIf before publishing. OPEN: does new-machine-tools go public (generic GUI tools) or private (if it accumulates work-specific tooling)?

tasks.title: Sanitize tracked .gitconfig before making repo public
tasks.notes: Repo is private, so real identities in tracked files are acceptable today. If it ever goes public: tracked .gitconfig holds user.email (dsuazop@gmail.com) and includeIf paths naming the raiz/blumar work trees; docs/gitconfig-conditional-includes.md additionally names all three GitHub accounts and both work email domains. Cheapest fix: move [user] out of the tracked .gitconfig into an untracked ~/.gitconfig-local pulled in via [include], mirroring how ~/.gitconfig-raiz and ~/.gitconfig-blumar already work — tracked file becomes structure only, no template/substitution step, symlink keeps working. The includeIf directory names (raiz/blumar) remain structural and can only be removed by untracking. Note .gitconfig is symlinked to ~/.gitconfig, so it cannot hold placeholders while also being the live config.

tasks.title: Set up Bitwarden CLI for personal credentials
tasks.notes: Bitwarden is already the password manager in use on Windows and phone; this is about getting it usable from the Linux CLI. Open decision: official 'bw' (Node, npm install -g @bitwarden/cli or native binary from releases - check 'zypper se bitwarden', likely not in openSUSE repos) vs 'rbw' (unofficial Rust client, much faster, has an unlock agent so you are not re-entering the master password constantly; third-party client for the password vault, which is its own trust call). Official bw is required for anything touching org/admin operations. Session handling is the main friction: bw needs BW_SESSION exported and it expires - do NOT put it in .bashrc, it is a live vault-unlock token. Distinct from aws-vault, which stays as-is for AWS only.

tasks.title: Explore Bitwarden CLI for programmatic secret retrieval
tasks.notes: Direction, not a settled plan: use the Bitwarden CLI as a general secret-retrieval layer in scripts instead of scattering tokens across dotfiles and .env files. Shape is 'bw get password NAME' / 'bw get item NAME | jq' inline at the point of use. Depends on bitwarden-cli-setup landing first (client choice + session/agent handling). Two habits worth establishing up front: never persist BW_SESSION in shell init, and prefer passing secrets inline to the single command that needs them over 'export TOKEN=$(bw get ...)', which exposes them to every child process - same reasoning as 'aws-vault exec'. Bitwarden could also be the source of truth for the AWS key (it syncs to phone/Windows, ~/.awsvault/keys never will), seeding 'aws-vault add' - but Bitwarden should NOT be in the hot path for AWS, since that would trade away aws-vault's short-lived STS sessions for a long-lived key in the environment.

tasks.title: Decide a policy on pinning vs tracking latest for installed tools
tasks.notes:
install.sh mixes pinning strategies with no stated rationale, and each new tool re-opens the question ad hoc.

Current state as of 2026-07-28: Nerd Fonts pins a version (v3.2.1, with a hand-maintained 'check releases' comment that will go stale). nvm pins its installer (v0.40.1) but then installs node via 'nvm install --lts' (unpinned). starship, uv, docker, zoxide and Claude Code all pipe unpinned curl installers. neovim/zellij/broot fetch 'latest' release tarballs on the apt path. Native packages via pkg_install inherit whatever the distro ships.

The tension: pinning gives reproducible machines and guards against a bad upstream release, but goes stale and needs manual bumping - the Nerd Fonts comment is already evidence of that cost. Tracking latest is self-maintaining but means two machines built a month apart differ, and a broken upstream release breaks a fresh install.

Wanted: a stated default (probably 'track latest unless there is a reason to pin'), the criteria for the exception, and where the pin lives so it is bumpable in one place rather than scattered through installer functions. Then reconcile the existing inconsistencies to match. Surfaced during duckdb-setup research (duckdb would add another unpinned 'curl | sh').

tasks.title: Make 'one line in links.sh' true for a new category
tasks.notes:
CLAUDE.md's 'When Adding New Configs' now says one `group:src:dest` line in links.sh covers linking, verification, and uninstall. That is exactly true for a config joining an EXISTING group, but a brand-new category still needs a gated `link_group <new>` block plus a matching `verify_group <new>` line in install.sh, because gating mirrors the INSTALL_* prompt flags. Flagged by goal-verifier on feat/uninstall-symlink-gaps (2026-07-28) as the one gap between the doc claim and reality.

Two ways out: (a) cheap — tighten the CLAUDE.md wording to say 'existing group' and document the extra install.sh step for a new category; (b) real — let links.sh carry the group->flag mapping so install.sh loops over groups generically and a new category is genuinely one registry edit. (b) subsumes (a) and kills the last hand-maintained list; (a) is a one-line doc edit if (b) is not worth it.

Not urgent: all 14 current links live in existing groups, so nothing is broken today. Bites the first time a new tool category is added.

tasks.title: backlog validate cites a rule file this repo doesn't have
tasks.notes:
`claude-toolkit backlog validate` caps task notes at 1300 chars and directs you to externalize the overflow to output/claude-toolkit/backlog-notes/<id>.md, 'see .claude/rules/workflow/backlog.md'. That rule file does not exist in this repo, and neither does the backlog-notes/ directory, so the externalization format is unspecified locally.

Hit while adding install-script-testing (2026-07-28): trimmed the notes twice to fit rather than invent a format. new-machine-tools has carried the same violation since it was written (1640 chars) and is why validate currently exits 1.

Resolve by either syncing the rule file from claude-toolkit (claude-sync) if it exists upstream, or documenting the externalization convention here and fixing new-machine-tools so validate exits clean.

tasks.title: Separate contributor dev-tooling from new-machine bootstrap
tasks.notes:
install.sh provisions a new machine; it is not the same requirement as being able to develop/test this repo. Conflating the two led to two concrete issues (2026-07-28):

1. bats-core was rejected for the test harness on the grounds that 'this repo bootstraps a machine, so its tests must run on a bare one'. That reasoning is wrong: testing happens on an already-set-up dev machine, so a dev-time test dependency is fine. The plain-bash harness that shipped is good and not worth rewriting, but the constraint should not block future tooling choices.

2. `make lint` now hard-requires shellcheck via a local pre-commit hook, and install.sh does NOT install shellcheck. A contributor on a fresh checkout gets 'Executable shellcheck not found' on their first commit, with nothing telling them why.

Decide the model: either a separate `make dev-setup` / documented contributor prerequisites (shellcheck, and anything future tooling wants), or add dev tools to install.sh behind their own category prompt so they are opt-in rather than part of a minimal machine. Then document which is which in CONTRIBUTING or README.

Fixing #2 is the concrete deliverable; #1 is the principle that prevents it recurring.

tasks.title: Decide whether shell config should be shellcheck-linted
tasks.notes:
The shellcheck pre-commit hook (v0.1.15) is scoped by a files: regex to install.sh, uninstall.sh, links.sh, tests/ and scripts/. Shell config — .bashrc, .aliases — is excluded.

Rationale for excluding: those files are sourced into an interactive shell, not executed, so SC2148 (no shebang) and SC1090 (can't follow non-constant source) are inherent to what they are rather than defects. A repo-wide hook fails on them immediately.

Caveat worth revisiting: when the exclusion was chosen, .bashrc could not be read in-session (a secrets guard blocks reading shell init files), so its 6 findings were never actually inspected — only 2 of the 6 were confirmed as the inherent SC2148/SC1090 kind from the hook's own output. The remaining 4 were SC1091 'not following' info for optional sourced files (cargo env, nvm, .local/bin/env), which look benign but were not verified line by line.

Options: (a) leave excluded and accept shell config is unlinted; (b) add  + targeted disable directives to .bashrc/.aliases and bring them into the hook; (c) lint them at a lower severity (-S warning) so the inherent findings drop out. Requires reading .bashrc, so it needs a session where that is permitted.
